Summary: OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit 76b95cf is reported vulnerable in the TCP explicit-messaging path (RegisterSession -> SendRRData). Issue: 582
Summary: OpENer 2.3.0 (commit 76b95cf) has an out-of-bounds read in CIP message parsing when handling malformed explicit requests with a forged EPath size. An ENIP SendRRData request can carry a very short CIP payload whose attacker-controlled path_size claims more path words than are actually available; because the parser continues decoding path segments without a remaining-length boundary, it reads past the end of the stack receive buffer. The report states this is remotely triggerable via network traffic and does not require authentication.
Reproduce: Use the provided Python 3 PoC against a target listening on 127.0.0.1:44818 by default (defaults: attempts=1, timeout=1.5, interval_ms=0, path_words=240, buffer_size=512). The client opens a TCP connection, sends ENIP RegisterSession (0x0065) with payload <HH>(1,0), and extracts the returned session ID. It then sends ENIP SendRRData (0x006F) for that session with 6 zero command-specific bytes plus a CPF whose item count is 3, containing a Null Address item (0x0000, length 0) and an Unconnected Data item (0x00B2) whose declared data length is only 2 bytes: service 0x0E followed by a forged path_size byte set to the requested path_words value. The PoC then appends repeated 0x20 0x01 bytes after that declared payload until the whole packet reaches 512 bytes, sends it, and waits for a reply. Reported outcomes are either RESP - response_len=... or FAIL - no response (reset, crash, or ASan abort), or an exception.

Issue: 567
Summary: On the latest master branch of OpENer, the report describes a remotely reachable server-side crash triggered by a crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request. The report attributes the underlying corruption to request handling before the visible crash: CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure() accepts a malformed CPF with an invalid item_count/inconsistent length, the unconnected Message Router payload reaches GetAttributeList(), GetAttributeList() parses an attacker-controlled excessively large attribute_count_request and builds an oversized inner Message Router response, and EncodeMessageRouterResponseData() copies that inner response into the outer ENIPMessage without validating remaining destination capacity. According to the report, this overruns message_buffer[512] and overwrites the adjacent current_message_position field; the observed result is that AddIntToMessage() later dereferences the corrupted pointer and crashes. The documented crash is an AddressSanitizer SEGV caused by a READ in AddIntToMessage() at source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c:136.
Reproduce: 1) Use the latest master branch of OpENer and run a server instance; the report demonstrates the issue on an AddressSanitizer-instrumented POSIX OpENer build. 2) Send the provided crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request to the server. The PoC is the hex byte sequence beginning with <6f><00><30><01><30><30><30><30> and continuing exactly as provided in the document. 3) Observe the server abort under AddressSanitizer with a SEGV caused by a READ in AddIntToMessage() at source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c:136:49, with the stack including EncodeSockaddrInfoItemTypeId(), AssembleLinearMessage(), NotifyCommonPacketFormat(), HandleReceivedSendRequestResponseDataCommand(), and HandleReceivedExplictTcpData().

Issue: 568
Summary: OpENer 2.3.0 (master branch up to commit 76b95cf) has an integer underflow in the connected explicit message path for SendUnitData. In `source/src/enet_encap/cpf.c`, `NotifyConnectedCommonPacketFormat` subtracts 2 from the connected data-item length without checking that it is at least 2; a length of 1 underflows to -1. That value is passed into `CreateMessageRouterRequestStructure` in `source/src/cip/cipmessagerouter.c`, decremented again, and later bypasses a bounds check because the signed length is compared after an implicit unsigned conversion. With a forged large `path_size`, `DecodePaddedEPath` can read far out of bounds from the `incoming_message` buffer, which the report describes as a stack buffer overflow and severe memory corruption.
Reproduce: Use the provided Python TCP client against the target host and port 44818 (default host 127.0.0.1). Each request uses a 24-byte header: `<HHII` command, payload length, session, 0, plus 12 null bytes. Connect with a 2s timeout; send Register Session (0x65) with payload `struct.pack('<HH', 1, 0)` and read the session ID from bytes 4-7 of the reply; send ForwardOpen (0x6F) on that session with the provided CIP/CPF bytes, then extract the connection ID from the reply at marker `\xD4\x00\x00\x00`; finally send SendUnitData (0x70) on the same session with CPF item `0x00A1`, that connection ID, and a connected data item `0x00B1` whose length is `1`, followed by one null byte and the forged path tail `\x41\x0e\xfa` plus `\x20\x02` repeated 232 times. The write-up says the trigger should hit the bug; if ASAN catches it, OpENer crashes.

Issue: 562
Summary: OpENer 2.3.0 (commit 76b95cf) is reported vulnerable to a Slowloris-style denial of service in its TCP/ENIP handling path. The report points to the single-threaded network loop in NetworkHandlerProcessCyclic(), where a newly accepted TCP socket from CheckAndHandleTcpListenerSocket() is added to the read set without being set non-blocking, and HandleDataOnTcpSocket() then performs blocking recv() calls. If a client opens one TCP connection, sends only the first 4 bytes of an ENIP packet so the server learns a payload length, and then withholds the rest of the packet, the subsequent recv() for the remaining data can block indefinitely until more data arrives or a TCP timeout occurs. The demonstrated impact is that the main network processing loop stalls and legitimate requests are not handled during that time.
Reproduce: Prerequisite: have an OpENer 2.3.0 server listening on TCP port 44818 (the PoC defaults to 127.0.0.1:44818). Use the provided Python PoC logic as follows: 1) Open a TCP socket to the target host and port. 2) Build an ENIP header for command 0x006F with a declared payload length (the PoC default is 128 bytes). 3) Send only the first 4 bytes of that header, which contain the ENIP command and length. 4) Keep the connection open and send no additional bytes; the PoC idles for 60 seconds by default. The documented expected result is that OpENer reads the first 4 bytes, derives data_size, then blocks in the next recv() inside HandleDataOnTcpSocket() while waiting for the undeclared remainder. Because this occurs inside the single-threaded NetworkHandlerProcessCyclic loop, other legitimate requests are not processed until data arrives or the TCP connection times out.

Issue: 575
Summary: OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit 76b95cf has a remotely reachable stack-use-after-return in the EtherNet/IP Common Packet Format (CPF) handling logic. The process-global CPF parsing state `g_common_packet_format_data_item` is reused across messages and protocol paths; `CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure()` only refreshes `data_item` when `item_count >= 2`, so a later CPF packet with `item_count == 1` updates only the address item and leaves the previous `data_item.type_id`, `data_item.length`, and `data_item.data` unchanged. A valid UDP I/O consuming packet can therefore populate `g_common_packet_format_data_item.data_item.data` with a pointer into the stack buffer of `CheckAndHandleConsumingUdpSocket()`, and a later TCP `SendUnitData` packet with only a `ConnectionAddress` item can reuse that stale UDP `data_item` in the TCP connected explicit path, causing `NotifyConnectedCommonPacketFormat()` to read from a returned UDP stack frame. The documented result on ASan builds is an `AddressSanitizer: stack-use-after-return` crash in `GetUintFromMessage`; the report states this is at minimum a remotely triggerable denial of service.

Issue: 571
Summary: In OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit `76b95cf`, `ParseConnectionPath()` in `source/src/cip/cipconnectionmanager.c` mishandles connection-path accounting during server-side `ForwardOpen` processing. The function tracks the path length in 16-bit words, but in the `kNetworkSegmentSubtypeProductionInhibitTimeInMilliseconds` branch it advances `message` by 2 bytes and subtracts `2` from `remaining_path`, even though that segment occupies only 2 bytes (1 word). When a crafted EtherNet/IP `ForwardOpen` places this Production Inhibit Time-in-milliseconds network segment as the last word of the connection path on a non-cyclic connection, `remaining_path` underflows from `1` to a very large `size_t` value. The parser then continues its `while (remaining_path > 0)` loop and calls `GetPathSegmentType()` on a pointer that has already advanced past the end of the received TCP message buffer. The documented observed result, with ASan/UBSan enabled, is a reproducible stack-based out-of-bounds read reported as `stack-buffer-overflow` / `READ of size 1` in `GetPathSegmentType()`.
Reproduce: Build and run the OpENer server with ASan/UBSan enabled, listening on EtherNet/IP TCP port 44818. Use the provided Python 3 PoC against that server; by default it targets `127.0.0.1:44818` and uses `crash` mode, or accepts `script.py [baseline|filler|crash] [host]`. In `crash` mode, the client: 1) opens a TCP connection to the server, 2) sends an EtherNet/IP `RegisterSession` request and reads the returned session handle, 3) builds a `SendRRData` packet carrying a CIP `ForwardOpen` request, 4) sets the connection path to the normal base path plus a 209-word simple data filler segment, then appends a trailing Production Inhibit Time in milliseconds network segment `0x43 0x01`

Issue: CVE-2020-13556
Summary: OpENer 2.3 and development commit 8c73bf3 have an out-of-bounds write in the Ethernet/IP server functionality, in source/src/enet_encap/cpf.c within CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure. The function reads item_count from an ENIP packet and uses it as a loop counter; during that loop, GetIntFromMessage reads two bytes, converts them to a short integer, and writes it into an array in common_packet_format_data, corresponding to the global g_common_packet_format_data_item, without validating that item_count stays within the valid address_info_item entries. A specially crafted sequence of network requests with an oversized item_count causes the loop to continue past valid entries, resulting in out-of-bounds reads and writes. The document states the write begins at g_common_packet_format_data_item in the .bss segment, can overwrite the heap, and could lead to remote code execution.
Reproduce: The document does not provide a full PoC, build configuration, or commands. The described reproduction is to run an affected OpENer 2.3 or development commit 8c73bf3 Ethernet/IP server and send a specially crafted sequence of ENIP network requests. In the request processed by CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure, set the ENIP packet's item_count field larger than the number of valid address_info_item entries. As the loop continues, GetIntFromMessage keeps reading two-byte values and writing them into the common_packet_format_data / g_common_packet_format_data_item array past its bounds. Expected result: out-of-bounds read/write starting at g_common_packet_format_data_item in the .bss segment; the document says this can overwrite the heap and could lead to remote code execution.

Issue: CVE-2021-21777
Summary: OpENer 2.3 and development commit 8c73bf3 contain an EtherNet/IP UDP handler integer-conversion bug in generic_networkhandler.c, involving CheckAndHandleUdpUnicastSocket, HandleReceivedExplictUdpData, and CreateEncapsulationStructure. CheckAndHandleUdpUnicastSocket passes received_size as a signed integer, and CreateEncapsulationStructure parses the 2-byte encapsulation length as a signed value and uses it in the returned length calculation. A UDP request with the 24-byte EtherNet/IP header and a malicious length around 0x8000 is treated as a negative short, so follow-up parsing can jump up to roughly 32000 bytes before the receive buffer and treat that memory as another command packet. If one of several possible matching opcodes is found there, the server can return bytes from that memory, causing an out-of-bounds read and information leak. The report also states that making the jump return to the packet start causes a 100% CPU loop, and that using such a request with a spoofed source IP and an opcode that results in a reply creates a continuous UDP reply stream to the spoofed victim.
Reproduce: 1) Start an affected OpENer server; the issue applies to UDP, and the report says a listening socket is opened by default on all available interfaces for broadcast mode. 2) Send a crafted EtherNet/IP UDP request with the 24-byte protocol header; after the 2-byte command code, set the 2-byte length field to a maliciously high value around 0x8000 so it is interpreted as a signed negative short. 3) After the packet is handled, the parser uses that signed length to move to a supposed follow-up request; instead, it can jump backward up to about 32000 bytes before the receive buffer and parse memory there as another command packet. 4) Information-disclo

Issue: 565
Summary: OpENer commit 76b95cf is reported to have incorrect access control in encapsulation-session handling. In encap.c, CheckRegisteredSessions() checks whether a supplied session_handle is active in the global session list, but not whether that handle belongs to the TCP socket that sent the request. The report says this weak check is used on critical command paths such as SendRRData and SendUnitData, and that UnregisterSession also tears down session resources based only on the handle. The report also describes this as session hijacking and cross-connection DoS; the demonstrated result shown is the forced disconnect of the legitimate client.

Issue: 557
Summary: OpENer’s explicit messaging path has a remotely reachable out-of-bounds read while decoding CIP padded EPath data. The document states that DecodePaddedEPath decodes attacker-controlled path segments before verifying that the declared path length is fully present in the buffer, and that the decoder does not receive remaining-buffer-length information and performs unchecked reads of *message_runner, message_runner + 1, and 16-bit values. After session registration, crafted SendRRData payloads trigger the fault; under ASan this is reported as a stack-buffer-overflow read in DecodePaddedEPath, and the process aborts, causing denial of service.
Reproduce: 1) Start the target exactly as shown in the document:
ASAN_OPTIONS="halt_on_error=1:abort_on_error=1:detect_leaks=0" UBSAN_OPTIONS="halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1" ./bin/posix-asan/src/ports/POSIX/OpENer lo
2) Use the provided Python 3 PoC against the target host (default 127.0.0.1) on TCP port 44818. The script defaults to MAX_TRIES=5000 and TIMEOUT=1.0.
3) For each attempt, open a TCP connection, send the fixed RegisterSession request 65000400000000000000000000000000000000000000000001000000, read the 24-byte reply, validate command 0x0065 with status 0, and extract the returned session ID.
4) Build and send a SendRRData packet (encapsulation command 0x006F) for that session. Its CPF payload contains a null address item and an unconnected data item 0x00B2 carrying a CIP payload of: service byte 0x0e, path_size byte 236, then 235 repetitions of the 8-bit logical segment bytes 0x20 0x01. Issue: 573
Summary: On OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf, the unconnected explicit TCP `SendRRData` path has a remotely reachable out-of-bounds read. `CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure()` recognizes optional sockaddr info items (`0x8000` / `0x8001`) and then reads the remaining fixed sockaddr fields without first checking that those bytes are still inside the received CPF buffer. The observed failure occurs before `NotifyMessageRouter()`, with the first invalid access in `GetIntFromMessage()`; ASan reports it as a stack-buffer-overflow crossing the right boundary of `incoming_message[512]` in `HandleDataOnTcpSocket()`.
Reproduce: Tested against OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit 76b95cf. The PoC is a Python 3 script that connects to TCP port 44818 on `OPENER_HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`), first sends a `RegisterSession` request (`0x0065`) and then a `SendRRData` request (`0x006F`). Run the script in `baseline` mode to send a normal CPF with a Null Address Item and an Unconnected Data Item, or in `crash` mode to send a 482-byte CPF whose last two bytes are `0x8000` so the packet ends with a recognized sockaddr info item. The crash case is: item count 3, Null Address Item, Unconnected Data Item length 470 filled with `A`, then trailing `0x8000`. Expected result: the target crashes before `NotifyMessageRouter()` is entered; the first invalid access is in `GetIntFromMessage()`, and ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow on `incoming_message[512]` in `HandleDataOnTcpSocket()`.

Issue: 572
Summary: In OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf, the real TCP explicit-message path on port 44818 (`RegisterSession` / `SendRRData`) can reach `SetAttributeList()` with a default-registered, non-settable `kCipShortString` attribute: Identity class, instance 1, attribute 7 (`product_name`). For non-settable attributes, `SetAttributeList()` still advances over the attacker-supplied value, and for variable-length types it calls `GetCipDataTypeLength(attribute->type, message_router_request->data)` without validating remaining length. For `kCipShortString`, that leads to an unchecked 1-byte read via `GetSintFromMessage()`. With a long padded EPath positioning `message_router_request->data` at the end of the 512-byte stack receive buffer, ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read. The document states this is at minimum a remote unauthenticated denial of service in the default build.
Reproduce: Use OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf with the default Ethernet buffer size (`PC_OPENER_ETHERNET_BUFFER_SIZE=512`). Start the server, then run the provided Python 3 PoC in `crash` mode against TCP port 44818 (default host `127.0.0.1`, override with `OPENER_HOST`). The script first sends `RegisterSession`, then `SendRRData` carrying a CIP `SetAttributeList` request to Identity class 1, instance 1, attribute 7. In crash mode it builds a long padded EPath (`build_path(233)`) and sends `attr_count=1`, `attr=7`, with no short-string length byte following the attribute id. Expected result: ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read when `SetAttributeList()` skips the non-settable short string value.

Issue: 570
Summary: A malformed `ForwardOpen` request can trigger a network-reachable out-of-bounds read in OpENer during connection-path parsing. In `ParseConnectionPath()`, the trailing Simple Data Segment length byte is trusted without checking that it still fits the remaining path budget, so `remaining_path` can underflow and `message` can be advanced past the request buffer. The next `GetPathSegmentType(message)` access then reads out of bounds and crashes the server. The reachable path shown is `HandleDataOnTcpSocket()` -> `HandleReceivedExplictTcpData()` -> `HandleReceivedSendRequestResponseDataCommand()` -> `NotifyCommonPacketFormat()` -> `NotifyMessageRouter()` -> `NotifyClass()` -> `ForwardOpen()` -> `ForwardOpenRoutine()` -> `HandleNonNullNonMatchingForwardOpenRequest()` -> `ParseConnectionPath()` -> `GetPathSegmentType()`. `HandleNonNullNonMatchingForwardOpenRequest()` calls `ParseConnectionPath()` before any `open_connection_function` is called.
Reproduce: Run the provided Python 3 PoC against an OpENer server listening on `127.0.0.1:44818`. The script registers a session, wraps a CIP `ForwardOpen` request to Connection Manager class `0x06`, instance `1`, inside `SendRRData`, and sends it over TCP 44818. It supports `baseline` and `crash`; `baseline` uses the valid path `20 04 24 97 2C 96 2C 64`, while `crash` appends `80 FF` so the trailing Simple Data Segment claims `0xff` words with only one word left. Command: `python3 poc.py crash`. On the vulnerable server, `ParseConnectionPath()` underflows `remaining_path`, advances past the request buffer, and `GetPathSegmentType()` dereferences out of bounds and crashes the server.
